complexity.notes: No hash structures, so worst case is genuinely O(n log n). The index recovery via repeated nums.index() calls is O(n) each (still dominated by the sort) and the pop/shift logic for duplicates is convoluted; a single pass with a value-to-index dict would give O(n) average time and be far more idiomatic.
complexity.summary: Sorts a copy of the array, uses a two-pointer scan to find the pair summing to target, then recovers the original indices via linear index() searches, with a pop-and-shift workaround when both elements share the same value.
